answer:
An agent in Loom is a role with one job, and it has its own model, prompt and tools. You can think of it as a function whose body is an LLM call. It reasons and writes text, and it can use the tools you give it.

Your project has one agent, `Helper`, on `gemini-2.5-flash`, with no tools. It can only read its input and write an answer. It can't touch anything outside the run.

The rule of thumb in the docs is that the model reads and your code decides and acts. Use an agent where you need text written. If a step only picks a label, use a classifier. If it calculates, checks a rule or moves money, use plain Java.

The next stage for your project is the harness. It's a short `HARNESS.md` that says how a run is bounded and what happens when it fails. Want me to explain that, or go deeper on agents, tools and effects first?
